cues.zh: 绵羊……并非一直都这么毛茸茸。
cues.en: Sheep... weren't always this fluffy.

cues.zh: 我们通过每一代都繁育最蓬松的个体，把它们变得毛茸茸。
cues.en: We fluffy-fied them by breeding the fluffiest in each generation.

cues.zh: 这就是驯化：为了人类更好地利用，而对野生动物进行塑造。
cues.en: This is domestication: sculpting wild animals for better human use.

cues.zh: 正如我们在第一部分看到的，对早期人类而言，动物是强大的工具
cues.en: As we saw in Part 1, for early man, animals were powerful tools

cues.zh: ……食物、衣物、交通、拖拉机。
cues.en: ...food, clothing, transportation, tractors.

cues.zh: 然而，尽管到处都有动物，在前现代世界里只有少数几种被驯化。
cues.en: Yet, though there were animals everywhere, only a handful were domesticated in the pre-modern world.

cues.zh: 是什么让这些动物与众不同？
cues.en: What made these different?

cues.zh: 我们来列一份驯化清单吧，好吗？
cues.en: Let's make a domestication checklist, shall we?

cues.zh: 第一项：可喂养
cues.en: First up: Feedable

cues.zh: 牛是一台把草变成牛排的机器
cues.en: A cow is a machine that turns grass into steaks

cues.zh: 而老虎是一台把牛排变成……老虎的机器。
cues.en: And a tiger a machine that turns steaks into… tiger.

cues.zh: 十磅草能产出一磅牛排。而十磅牛排能产出一磅老虎。
cues.en: Ten pounds of grass make a pound of steak. And ten pounds of steak make a pound of tiger.

cues.zh: ……但这两者的卡路里数相同——所以你还不如直接吃牛，省下大量功夫。
cues.en: ... but these have the same number of calories -- so you might as well just eat the cow and save yourself a lot of work.

cues.zh: 所以纯肉食动物：因为热力学的原因，你根本驯化不了它们。
cues.en: So pure carnivores: you're not going to domesticate, just because of thermodynamics.

cues.zh: 你要找的是不挑食的食草动物。
cues.en: You're looking for herbivores that aren't picky.

cues.zh: 它们应该吃那些到处都是、你又吃不了的东西。
cues.en: They should eat something that's everywhere that you can't eat.

cues.zh: 任何杂食动物最好什么都乐意吃，而且最好超级划算。
cues.en: Any omnivores better be happy eating whatever and better be super worth it.

cues.zh: 不过，我们这里是把猪放在猪圈前面了，因为首先得抓到某种……
cues.en: We are, however, putting the pig before the pen here because first we need to catch something that's…

cues.zh: 友好的东西。
cues.en: Friendly

cues.zh: 好吧，显然抓肉食动物本来就是个坏主意，因为它们的主业就是杀戮。
cues.en: OK, obviously catching a carnivore is a bad idea anyway because their day job is murder.

cues.zh: 但很多杂食动物，比如灰熊，也会兼职干杀戮这行。
cues.en: But plenty of omnivores like grizzleys moonlight in murder.

cues.zh: 素食者也不安全：水牛就是可怕的坦克，原因前面都提过了……
cues.en: No safety in vegetarians either: buffalo are terrifying tanks for all the reasons mentioned before...

cues.zh: ……河马在非洲保持着杀戮最高纪录，
cues.en: ...hippos hold the murder high-score in Africa,

cues.zh: ……长颈鹿看着挺呆的，直到你考虑到它们的攻击范围——狮子基本都不招惹它们。
cues.en: ...giraffes look real dorky until you consider their striking range -- lions mostly leave them alone.

cues.zh: 有些动物要是能驯化就太棒了，而它们恰好都超级危险。
cues.en: Animals it would be awesome to domesticate are, not coincidentally, super dangerous.

cues.zh: 战熊对你的部落来说绝对是巨大优势，但这不可能实现。
cues.en: War bears would be a hell of an advantage for your tribe, but it's not going to happen.

cues.zh: 而如果它体型大又不危险，那就是个神经兮兮的家伙。
cues.en: And if it's big and not dangerous, it's a nervous wreck.

cues.zh: 想偷偷靠近一只瞪羚？呵呵，想得美。
cues.en: Try sneaking up on a gazelle? Rhymes with "LOL".

cues.zh: 当然，你和一帮哥们可以花一整天马拉松式地追它，直到它精疲力竭……
cues.en: Sure, you and a team of buddies could spend the whole day marathon jogging it down to exhaustion...

cues.zh: ……但如果它在你试图拖它回家时没把自己的脖子折断，
cues.en: ...but if it doesn't break it's own neck as you try to drag it back home,

cues.zh: ……那它就会轻巧地跳出你给它建的任何围栏。
cues.en: ...then it's going to casually leap out of whatever pen you built for it.

cues.zh: 好，接下来：有些动物在繁殖方面有——啊——偏好……
cues.en: Ok, next up: some animals have reproductive -ah- preferences...

cues.zh: ……这让它们无法适应圈养。说的就是你，熊猫。
cues.en: ...that make them incompatible with captivity. Looking at you, Pandas.

cues.zh: 人类为了让熊猫愿意交配所花费的时间和精力，简直滑稽。
cues.en: The time and energy humans have spent to get pandas to get on with it is comical.

cues.zh: 狩猎采集者需要一种特别渴望繁殖的动物，以至于有时会搞错。
cues.en: Hunter-Gatherers need an animal so eager to breed, it gets it wrong sometimes.

cues.zh: ……而不是一种他们得小心追踪其交配季节的动物。
cues.en: ... not an animal whose mating seasons they have to keep careful track of.

cues.zh: 所以：友好、可喂养，还有——多产。
cues.en: So: Friendly, Feedable and -- Fecund.

cues.zh: 它还需要快速长大。
cues.en: It also needs to grow up fast.

cues.zh: 这就引出了驯化与驯服的核心区别。
cues.en: This gets us to the heart of domestication versus taming.

cues.zh: 再说一遍：驯化一个物种，就是改变它，让它对我们更有用。
cues.en: Again: to domesticate a species is to change it to make it better for us.

cues.zh: 顺便说一句：我们也驯化植物。
cues.en: And side note here: we domesticate plants as well.

cues.zh: 我们把它们培育成了野生祖先的怪物版本。
cues.en: We've bred them to be monstrous versions of their wild selves.

cues.zh: 所以当嬉皮士谈论回归自然时，他们忘了这些植物和这个果酱馅饼一样，都是人造的。
cues.en: So when hippies talk about going back to nature, they forget that these plants are just as man made as this pop-tart.

cues.zh: 总之，回到动物……
cues.en: Anyway, back to the animals...

cues.zh: 猪的“猪肉化”项目之所以成功，是因为猪的世代比人类短。
cues.en: The pig porkification project succeeded because pig generations are shorter than human generations.

cues.zh: 一个聪明人单打独斗，一辈子也只能取得缓慢的进展。
cues.en: A single, clever human can make porky progress in their lifetime.

cues.zh: 对比一下：大象。
cues.en: Compare and contrast: Elephants.

cues.zh: 两年才能生一头小象，两胎之间隔五年，雌象要九年才成年，雄象要十五年？
cues.en: Two years to make a calf, five years in between calves, nine years until female maturity, fifteen years for males?

cues.zh: 开什么玩笑，大象。这哪等得起。
cues.en: You've got to be kidding, Elephants. There's no time for this.

cues.zh: 但人类还是能驯服大象。你可以抓住一头大象，训练它别在人类身边惊慌。然后让它干活。
cues.en: But humans can still tame elephants. You can catch an elephant, and train it not to freak out around humans. Then, put it to work.

cues.zh: 但驯化大象需要跨越好几个人一生的准确记录……
cues.en: But elephant domestication would require accurate records over several human lives...

cues.zh: 更别说养一两头驯服的大象成本高得离谱
cues.en: ...never mind that keeping one or two tamed elephants around is incredibly costly

cues.zh: 这就是为什么战象只在已经相当复杂的社会里偶尔出现。
cues.en: ...which is why war elephants only happened on occasion in already complex societies.

cues.zh: 驯服的大象是奢侈品，所以有这么一条经验法则：在农场里的，是驯化；在马戏团里的，是驯服。
cues.en: Tame elephants are a luxury, hence this rule of thumb: if it's on farm, it's domesticated, if it's in a circus, it's tame.

cues.zh: 最后：家族。
cues.en: Finally: families.

cues.zh: 好，斑马与马。
cues.en: OK: zebra vs horses.

cues.zh: 马是文明的颠覆者——想想看，从公元前几千年直到电报出现……
cues.en: Horses are civilization game-changers -- it's remarkable to think that from thousands BC until the telegraph...

cues.zh: ……骑马的人就是当时最好的互联网。
cues.en: ...a dude on a horse was the best internet available.

cues.zh: 马是在欧亚大陆被驯化的，但人类起源于非洲，那里有斑马……
cues.en: Horses were domesticated in Eurasia, but humans started in Africa which has Zebra ...

cues.zh: ……为什么最早的人类没有骑着斑马走出非洲、征服世界呢？
cues.en: ...why didn't the first humans ride out of Africa on the backs of zebra to conquer the world?

cues.zh: 因为斑马是混蛋。它们生来就爱踢爱咬：在前青霉素时代很危险。
cues.en: Because zebra are bastards. They live to kick and bite: dangerous in a pre-penicillin world.

cues.zh: ……而且斑马还有闪避反射，让人很难套住它们。
cues.en: ...and zebra also have a ducking reflex making them very frustrating to lasso.

cues.zh: 斑马不仅是非常难搞的动物，还缺乏家族结构。
cues.en: In addition to being a real pain in the ass animal, Zebra lack a family structure.

cues.zh: 马群有等级制度——它们排成一列行进时就能看出来：公马、头号母马、她的幼驹、二号母马、她的幼驹，以此类推。
cues.en: Horse herds hierarchy -- you can see it when they travel in a line: the male, top female, her foals, second female, her foals, and so on.

cues.zh: 人类通过捕获并驯服领头公马，成为马群之首。
cues.en: Humans, by capturing and taming the lead male, become head horse.

cues.zh: 许多农场动物之所以成为农场动物，是因为它们有可供人类利用的家庭价值观——
cues.en: Lots of barnyard animals are barnyard animals because they have family values humans exploit --

cues.zh: ……它们从小就觉得，这个人类不过是一头有点滑稽的、爱管事的奶牛之类的。没什么大不了的。
cues.en: ...they just grow up with the idea that this human is a funny sort of take-charge cow or whatever. No big deal.

cues.zh: 鸡会啄、啄、啄，直到啄出谁是鸡群之首。
cues.en: Chickens will peck, peck, peck until they've worked out who's top chicken.

cues.zh: 但你知道谁才是真正的鸡群之首吗？我们才是。
cues.en: But you know whose really top chicken? We're top chicken.

cues.zh: 狗和猫：这正是它们的不同之处。
cues.en: Dogs and cats: this is what makes them different.

cues.zh: 狗会爱你、保护你、和你一起打猎，因为你是族群的一员。
cues.en: Dogs will love you and defend you and hunt with you because you're part of the pack.

cues.zh: 狗活着就是为了对我们有用——在现代世界里，这意味着倒地装死——但它们乐在其中
cues.en: Dogs live to be useful to us -- which in the modern world means falling over to play dead -- but they love it

cues.zh: “砰！……好姑娘。好姑娘！”[笑]
cues.en: "Bang! .... Good girl. Good girl!" [laughing]

cues.zh: ……而猫，则是一只住在你家里的小老虎。
cues.en: ... whereas a cat is a tiny tiger that lives in your house.

cues.zh: 好，回到这些家伙。
cues.en: Ok, back to these guys.

cues.zh: 对斑马来说，根本不存在社会这回事。
cues.en: For zebra, there's no such thing as society.

cues.zh: 它们成群结队是因为这是种不错的生存策略，但它们其实并不在乎彼此。
cues.en: They hang out in groups because it's a good survival strategy but they don't really care.

cues.zh: 抓住一匹斑马，它的家人不会跟来；想骑它，能保住手指就算走运了。
cues.en: Catch a zebra and his family won't follow, try to ride him and you'll be lucky to keep your fingers.

cues.zh: 斑马外表像马，内里可不是。
cues.en: Zebra look like horses on the outside, but not on the inside.

cues.zh: 所以这就是那份清单：温顺——可喂——多产——顾家
cues.en: So that's the checklist: Friendly - Feedable - Fecund - Family Friendly

cues.zh: 清单不长，但对狩猎采集者来说，他们想驯化的任何动物都得样样达标，……
cues.en: It's not a long checklist, but for Hunter-Gatherers, any animal they wanted to domesticate needed everything,...

cues.zh: ……这就是为什么在人类早期历史中，全世界只驯化了十几种大型动物。
cues.en: ...which is why in early human history only a bakers dozen of big animals were domesticated the world over.
